newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CONFRAM TO BUY 19.3 PCT OF ROMATEX.
newsitem.headline: CONFRAM TO BUY 19.3 PCT OF ROMATEX.

text.p: South Africa's Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd (Confram) said on Monday it would buy 19.3 percent of textile competitor Romatex at a price of 225 cents a Romatex share.

Confram would buy the Romatex stake from Romatex parent C.G. Smith Ltd ~CGSJn.J~which would in turn have acquired the shares from Associated Furniture Companies Ltd (Afcol) , the companies said in a statement on Monday.
Following the acquisition, Afcol would hold no shares in Romatex.
Confram would then extend an offer to Romatex shareholders to buy 38.0 percent of their shareholding at 225 cents per Romatex ordinary share, the statement said.
C.G. Smith has undertaken to accept the offer in respect of the remaining Romatex shares that it holds after the initial acquisition.
Following the various acquisitions Confram will end up with a 50.8 percent stake in Romatex bought for a total cash consideration of 28.6 million rand, the statement said.
Depending on the acceptance of the offer by other Romatex shareholders, C.G. Smith will retain a stake in Romatex of between 28.9 and 36.6 percent.
The Romatex disposal represents an important step in the further rationalisation of C.G. Smith's peripheral interests in the textile and floorcoverings sectors, the statement said.

It said the offer of 225 cents a Romatex share represents a discount to the closing price of 330 cents a share on Friday September 13. Romatex shareholders were last week cautioned that any bid for the company would be at less than 330 cents a share.

The statement said the discount reflects the trading performance of Romatex during the current finanical year and that in the year to September 30, 1996 it is expected to show a significant reduction in profits.
It said Romatex is expected to trade at a small loss for the second six month period and final earnings will only be slightly above breakeven.
Full year results will be announced on October 31, 1996.
Romatex shares listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange were last week on a rollercoaster ride on reports the firm is to be sold to Confram.

Early in the week shares surged on news of the planned sale, but on Thursday dived as much as 40 percent to an intraday low of 330 cents after Romatex said any bid for it would be at less than that price.
Shares closed on Friday at 330 cents a share following the Competition Board's preliminary approval of the merger with Confram.
